column1: # Worked-example acronym registry (@PLN141) — maps a tag acronym to the repo that
# owns it, so a `// Example: @AAA-###` citation resolves to a real test/function and
# produces a real link.  Tab-separated: acronym <TAB> local_path <TAB> git_url <TAB> branch
#   local_path   where the repo is checked out relative to THIS repo (`.` = loft
#                itself); `-` = no local checkout expected (validate/link online).
#   git_url      the repo's web root, used to build the actual link.
#   branch       the branch the tags live on (for the link + online validation).
# Resolution: if local_path is a directory, the tag is validated against that
# checkout (offline, authoritative) — this is preferred over online.  A cross-repo
# acronym with no checkout present is reported unvalidated (a warning), never a hard
# failure, so CI stays deterministic; the link is still emitted from git_url.
# The acronym namespace is ecosystem-global: one acronym names one repo everywhere.
